headline: Steady growth continues, but occupancy dips slightly
summary_short: Extra Space Storage reported Q2 2026 revenue of $874.2M (+3.9% y/y, +2.1% q/q) and diluted EPS of $1.25 (+5.9% y/y), while same-store NOI grew 3.5% y/y even as same-store occupancy slipped 20bp to 94.2%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 3.9% y/y to $874.2M on 2025/H1-2026 acquisitions, higher average rent per occupied square foot, and growth in tenant-reinsurance and management income. Same-store NOI grew 3.5% y/y even as occupancy eased 20bp to 94.2%. Property-operations expense rose 1.8% y/y on the same acquisition growth, partly offset by cost control outside property taxes and insurance. Net income rose 5.5% y/y to $263.5M; diluted EPS was $1.25 (+5.9% y/y). FFO reached $457.3M, up from $439.3M. Cash rose to $695.2M from $138.9M at year-end as operating cash flow outpaced investing and financing outflows; equity fell to $13,257.9M as dividends outpaced earnings. No forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Growth came from 2025/H1-2026 store acquisitions and higher average rent per occupied square foot; same-store NOI still rose 3.5% y/y even as same-store occupancy eased slightly and dividends continued to outpace net income.

Property rental revenue rose from acquisitions completed in 2025 and H1 2026 (partly offset by dispositions) and higher average annual rent per occupied square foot; management-fee and tenant-reinsurance income grew as managed stores rose to 4,410 from 4,179.

This is the release's 'Property operations' line. Its y/y rise was due to portfolio growth from acquisitions, partially offset by expense control in most categories except property taxes and insurance. The release gives no q/q commentary (10-Qs compare only to the prior year).

Operating income rose as total revenue growth (+3.9% y/y) outpaced total expense growth (+3.3% y/y); the release does not discuss operating income as a distinct line beyond its revenue/expense components.
Pretax income tracked the operating-income gain; interest expense was roughly flat y/y while interest income fell and income tax expense rose modestly, per the statement of operations.
Net income growth followed the pretax-income gain; the release attributes the period's income-tax increase specifically to higher book income and fewer permanent tax deductions on stock awards.
EPS growth (+5.9% y/y) reflects net income growth of 5.5% against a weighted diluted share count up ~4.0% y/y (220.4M vs 211.9M); the release does not explain the share-count change.
Mirrors the diluted EPS move above; basic and diluted EPS were identical in both periods presented.

Cash built up over H1 2026 as operating cash flow ($1,076.3M) exceeded combined investing and financing outflows (-$175.8M, -$343.8M) per the MD&A cash-flow summary; the release does not single out a specific cause for the cash balance itself.
Equity declined as H1 2026 dividends paid ($684.7M) exceeded H1 net income ($528.3M) and modest buybacks; not framed as a specific driver in the release.
